$meta.how: get_variable_defs for primitive hexes and the type ramp; get_design_context on node 51:10 (06 Semantic colors) for the light/dark alias table
$meta.rule: This file is the Figma export. src/tokens.css and src/lib/tokens.js are GENERATED from it by scripts/build-tokens.mjs. Never hand-edit the generated files; re-extract and regenerate instead.

semantic.$note: Values are ALIASES into primitives, exactly as the Figma 06 Semantic colors page documents them. The resolver in build-tokens.mjs dereferences them per mode.

type.$note: Inter. This ramp is the authority — 10/12/14/16/18/20/28/32/56 at weights 400/500/600/700. Sizes 24 and 40 do not exist in this system; do not introduce them.

schemes.$provenance: MIXED PROVENANCE. `default` and `sunset` are the real Figma blue and orange ramps. The other seven are GENERATED in build-tokens.mjs from a base hue, using one monotonic lightness curve, because the design file has not published a colour-scheme foundation page. Replace them when it does.
schemes.$rule: A scheme changes the BRAND HUE ONLY. Neutrals, surfaces, text, borders and the status ramps never change — a colour scheme must not be able to break contrast or restyle a warning.

fonts.$provenance: Inter is the design-system face and the default. The alternates are a shell preference, not a design-system choice — they change the body face only, never the ramp.

nonFigma.$provenance: NOT from Figma. The colour page is the only foundations page published so far. These come from docs/admin-layout-guide.md, where every value was measured from the Genus WFM source. Replace with Figma values when the spacing/radius/elevation/motion foundation pages ship.

components.$note: TIER 3 — component tokens. `$base` holds slots shared by every variant and state; `$variants` → `$states` holds the ones that change. Alias forms: {sem:surface/raised} · {space:4} · {radius:surface} · {type:label/m} · {layout:drawerWidth} · {mix:role,over,pct} for a translucent tint composited to an opaque hex. A bare number or string is a literal, which is a smell worth questioning.
components.$rule: A colour slot MUST NOT alias a primitive directly — that skips the only tier that knows about light and dark. A state named `disabled` is auto-exempt under WCAG 1.4.3. Every state carrying both `fg` and `bg` is auto-paired for contrast, so declaring a state declares its coverage.

kpiTile.$note: The dashboard metric card. Six sit side by side, so its padding and min-height set the rhythm of every overview screen.

border.$note: border/subtle and surface/raised are the SAME hex in dark mode — a 1.00:1 edge. Hence the dark override; see AGENTS.md §1.

unsetColor.$note: A value the platform cannot state. Italic in this colour, never a plausible zero.

panel.$note: The standard bordered section. Every table and chart in the product sits in one.

button.$note: Five variants, five states each. The contained variants' label is DERIVED per fill (AGENTS.md §1a) — the `fg` slots below record what that derivation currently produces, so the audit can score them.

$knownDefect.note: The contained label is derived from the REST fill, but hover and pressed are different fills — and in light mode the ramp spans the luminance point where the required foreground flips. One label cannot serve all three. Same root cause as §0.6; fixing it means changing the light-mode interaction ramp.

THE BRAND COLOUR USED AS 14px TEXT. In dark mode action/primary/rest is ramp[400], chosen so the brand works as a FILL and as a 3:1 non-text indicator. As a label it needs 4.5:1 and delivers 4.08:1 on surface/raised — so every outlined button, text button, active nav row and selected tab label is non-compliant in dark mode, in all nine schemes. 81 instances, one cause. The fix mirrors what focus/ring already does: derive a separate brand-as-text step, the first clearing 4.5:1 against the hardest surface (blue-300 gives 5.63:1). That changes shipped colour, so it needs sign-off.
$knownDefect.decision: token-engine-architecture.md §5.6 — the fill/indicator split, now three roles: fill, indicator, text

button.$borderNote: An outlined button's edge is the only thing identifying it — SC 1.4.11 applies. Uses border/strong, not border/default: default is 1.69:1 against the fill and cannot be seen.

input.$note: Outlined text field. Five states, and `error` is a state rather than a variant because it is transient.
input.$borderNote: A field's boundary is what says 'you may type here'. SC 1.4.11 applies. Uses border/strong for the same reason.

navItem.$note: Sidebar row. `active` uses a brand tint over the rail surface — declared as a mix so its contrast is judgeable.

navItem.$borderNote: Nav rows carry no edge; selection is a tint plus weight.

tableRow.$note: Grid rows. Density comes from `layout.row*`; these are the paint states.
tableRow.$borderNote: Row rules are separators, not control boundaries.

tab.$note: Tab bar. `selected` carries both a colour and the indicator, so colour is never the only signal.

tab.$borderNote: The selected tab is identified by its indicator and label colour, not by an edge.

statusChip.$note: Five tones. Colour is never the only signal — each chip carries a word, and the band ones an icon too.
statusChip.$borderNote: Chips are identified by fill and word, never by an outline.

bandChip.$note: The band system's five states. `normal` is intentionally colourless — emphasis is zero-sum, and a grid where every cell is tinted has no exceptions left to notice (AGENTS.md §2).

freshnessChip.$note: How old a reading is. Four states, because 'stale' and 'offline' are different facts.

dialog.$note: Modal surface. Sits on `surface/overlay`, which is a distinct role from `raised` on purpose.

tooltip.$note: Deliberately inverted — a tooltip that matches its surroundings reads as part of the page.

pageHeader.$note: Owns the single h1. Panel titles are h2 inside PanelHeader.

emptyState.$note: Four different nothings need four different sentences — the title names the condition.

codeValue.$note: Raw device codes. Monospaced so a technician can read a hex register without transcription errors.
